name: Substack
description: Read a Substack publication: list, search and open posts, read comments and the RSS feed, and find a writer's publication from their @handle. 7 read-only tools, no API key.
instructions:
This connector reads one Substack publication through the public JSON endpoints its own website uses (Substack has no documented public API). Everything is read-only and needs no key; paid-only posts show their preview, not the full text.

**Getting credentials**: none. Set `SUBSTACK_PUBLICATION_URL` to the publication's home address, nothing after the domain: `https://yourname.substack.com` or a custom domain such as `https://www.lennysnewsletter.com`. A profile link (`https://substack.com/@handle`), a note link (`https://substack.com/@handle/note/c-123`) or a post link does not work. To find the address from a profile: open `substack.com/@handle`, click the publication shown on the profile, and copy the address bar up to the domain. In an app share link `open.substack.com/pub/NAME/p/...`, `NAME` is the subdomain: use `https://NAME.substack.com`. A `*.substack.com` address of a publication with a custom domain is redirected and also works.

**Workflow**: `substack_list_posts` first (newest, or `sort=top` for most liked). Then `substack_get_post_by_id` with a post `id`, or `substack_get_post_by_slug` with the part after `/p/` in a post link, for the full `body_html`. `substack_get_comments` reads the discussion. `substack_find_publication_by_handle` turns an @handle into the writer's publication subdomain and custom domain.

**Formats and gotchas**: dates are ISO 8601 UTC. `audience` is `everyone`, `only_paid`, `founding` or `only_free`. A 404 on every tool means there is no publication at the configured address; an HTML page instead of JSON means the address is a profile or a non-Substack site.

**Pagination and limits**: list and search tools take `limit` (1 to 50, the API rejects more) and `offset`; page with `offset` += `limit` until fewer than `limit` posts come back. Substack publishes no rate limit; keep to about one request per second.

**Cloud reachability**: all `*.substack.com` addresses, custom domains and `substack.com` are public HTTPS, reachable from AnythingMCP Cloud and from self-hosted installs with internet access.

SUBSTACK_PUBLICATION_URL.label: Publication URL
SUBSTACK_PUBLICATION_URL.help: The publication's home address, nothing after the domain: https://yourname.substack.com or its custom domain. A profile (substack.com/@handle) links to the publication: open it there and copy the address bar up to the domain.
SUBSTACK_PUBLICATION_URL.patternMessage: Use the publication's home address with https:// and nothing after the domain, e.g. https://yourname.substack.com or https://www.yournewsletter.com. A profile (substack.com/@handle), note or post link does not work: open the publication from the profile and copy its address up to the domain.

verifyHints.404: There is no Substack publication at this address. Use the publication's home address (https://yourname.substack.com or its custom domain), not a profile, note or post link.

tools.name: substack_list_posts
tools.description: List the publication's posts, newest first or most liked first. Each post has id, title, subtitle, slug, post_date, audience (everyone/only_paid/founding/only_free), type (newsletter/podcast/thread), wordcount, reaction_count, comment_count, canonical_url and a short truncated_body_text. Use substack_get_post_by_id for the full text.

limit.description: Posts per page, 1 to 50 (Substack rejects more). Default 12.

offset.description: Number of posts to skip, for the next page: previous offset + limit.

sort.description: new = most recent first (default), top = most liked first.

tools.name: substack_search_posts
tools.description: Full-text search the publication's post archive. Returns matching posts newest first, same fields as substack_list_posts (id, title, slug, post_date, audience, type). An empty array means nothing matched.

query.description: Words to search for in post titles and text.

offset.description: Number of results to skip, for the next page.

tools.name: substack_get_post_by_id
tools.description: Fetch one post by its numeric id, with the full body_html (a preview only for paid posts), subtitle, post_date, audience, comment_count and podcast_url for audio posts. The answer has the post under `post` and the publication's name and settings under `publication`.

postId.description: Numeric post id from substack_list_posts or substack_search_posts.

tools.name: substack_get_post_by_slug
tools.description: Fetch one post by its slug, the part after /p/ in a post link (for https://name.substack.com/p/my-first-post the slug is my-first-post). Returns the post with id, title, post_date, audience and the full body_html (a preview only for paid posts).

slug.description: Post slug, e.g. my-first-post. Only the part after /p/, without the domain or query string.

tools.name: substack_get_comments
tools.description: Get the comments on a post, as threads: each comment has id, name, handle, date, body, reaction_count and its replies under children. Best comments first by default.

tools.name: substack_get_rss_feed
tools.description: Fetch the publication's RSS 2.0 feed (/feed): the most recent posts with title, link, publication date and HTML content. Paid posts carry only a preview.

tools.name: substack_find_publication_by_handle
tools.description: Look up a Substack writer by @handle (from a profile link substack.com/@handle) and return their name, bio and the publications they write for, with subdomain and custom_domain. The publication address is https://<custom_domain> when set, otherwise https://<subdomain>.substack.com. Works for any writer, not only the configured publication.

handle.description: The handle without @, e.g. lenny for substack.com/@lenny.
